candidates.name: Shinsaibashi-suji Shopping Street
candidates.why: The covered spine of Minami shopping, about 600 m from Nagahoribashi down to Dotonbori: drugstores (Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Daikoku, Sundrug side by side for price comparison), Uniqlo/GU, ABC-Mart, sneaker and character shops, plus Daimaru Shinsaibashi and Shinsaibashi PARCO at the north end. Covered, so it works in December rain. A 2026 Xiaohongshu guide treats Shinsaibashi + Namba as the main shopping zone in Osaka. It is the classic route and is worth doing, but walk it in the morning before the crowds peak and do the vintage shopping in Amerikamura, one block west.
candidates.best_time: Weekday 11:00–14:00, before the evening crowd; walk it north to south so you finish at Dotonbori
candidates.price: Free to walk; drugstore haul ¥5,000–15,000 pp is typical (aim for ¥5,000+ excl. tax at one store, on one day, for tax-free)
candidates.group_of_8: Split into 2–4s and meet at Daimaru's main entrance or Ebisubashi; the street is too packed to move as 8

evidence.note: Updated 2026 guide to the Shinsaibashi + Namba shopping area: department stores, cosmetics, streetwear and second-hand in one zone
Says Osaka is very easy to shop, with Shinsaibashi and Umeda as the two centres

candidates.name: Amerikamura (Ame-mura) vintage streets around Triangle Park
candidates.name_ja: アメリカ村（三角公園周辺）
candidates.why: Osaka's youth-fashion and vintage district, just west of Midosuji. Guides count around 2,500 shops, and budget-friendly vintage clusters within a few blocks of Triangle Park (Mitsu Park). Good budget picks: Grizzly Ame-mura 1st/2nd (Ralph Lauren and street), Mecca (30s–60s American denim), Pigsty, and the WEGO/streetwear shops. This is the best part of Osaka for this group: cheap, walkable, photogenic, with takoyaki stands by the park. A 2025 Xiaohongshu poster warns vintage has got pricier than two years ago, but the shops are dense enough to compare.
candidates.best_time: 13:00–19:00. Many vintage shops open at noon or 13:00, and a few close Wednesdays (e.g. Mecca)
candidates.price: Chain thrift ¥300–1,000 per piece, mid-range ¥2,000–8,000, curated vintage ¥5,000–30,000+
candidates.group_of_8: Meet at Triangle Park, scatter into small groups for 2 hours, regroup there

candidates.name: Kinji used clothing (Big Step 2F)
candidates.name_ja: KINJI アメリカ村店（ビッグステップ2F）
candidates.why: A large, cheap used-clothing floor inside the Big Step building, the landmark mall at the Shinsaibashi end of Ame-mura. It mixes pre-owned designer pieces with cheap vintage, and the chain is known in Tokyo and Kyoto for low racks. It is the easiest first stop for 8 people on a budget, and Big Step itself has more youth brands and a WEGO nearby.
candidates.best_time: Start here at 12:00 when it opens, before the Triangle Park loop
candidates.group_of_8: Big floor; the whole group fits

candidates.name: Mandarake Grand Chaos
candidates.name_ja: まんだらけ グランドカオス
candidates.why: A multi-floor second-hand otaku store in Ame-mura, not Den Den Town: figures, vintage manga, doujinshi, retro game software, cels and toys. Better than most Nipponbashi shops for out-of-print and character goods. It fits naturally into the vintage loop, so the anime fans can split off for an hour.
candidates.group_of_8: Narrow aisles; send the 2–4 who care

candidates.name: Horie Orange Street (Tachibana-dori) · JAM Horie
candidates.name_ja: 堀江オレンジストリート（立花通り）・JAM 堀江店
candidates.why: About 800 m of independent fashion, sneaker, furniture and vintage shops, roughly 3 minutes' walk west of Triangle Park, and the closest shopping street to Kujō House. JAM is a budget vintage warehouse with about 9,000 items. jaBBer (LA buys, occasional low-price sales) and LARA Vintage (European vintage) are on the same street. It is calmer and more local than Ame-mura, a good way to finish the Minami loop heading home toward Nishi-ku.
candidates.group_of_8: Easy; wide street, shops big enough for 8

candidates.name: Den Den Town · Ota Road (Super Potato, Animate, card shops)
candidates.name_ja: でんでんタウン・オタロード（日本橋）
candidates.why: Osaka's Akihabara, a 10-minute walk south-east of Namba. Ota Road, one block west of Sakaisuji, is the core. Super Potato Retrokan (retro consoles and boxed games, a famous stop), Animate's Nipponbashi flagship, Surugaya, K-Books, Toranoana, Volks, Yellow Submarine for trading cards, gachapon lines and Taito Station cranes. It is cheaper and less crowded than Akihabara. Sofmap and Joshin do tax-free electronics.
candidates.best_time: Weekday 11:00–14:00; shops open 10:00–11:00. Pair with Namba Parks next door
candidates.price: Gachapon ¥100–400 (premium ¥1,000–2,000); retro carts from a few hundred yen
candidates.group_of_8: Works as a group stroll; split up inside shops

candidates.name: Namba Parks
candidates.why: A terraced mall above Nankai Namba with a rooftop garden. It is mostly mid-range chains and lifestyle brands, so it is less useful for this group than Ame-mura or Den Den Town. Worth 30–45 minutes only because it sits between Namba station and Den Den Town: walk the rooftop terraces and check the outdoor and sports shops. Skip it if time is tight.
candidates.best_time: Late morning on the way to Den Den Town, or at dusk for the lit terraces

candidates.name: Don Quijote Dotonbori
candidates.name_ja: ドン・キホーテ 道頓堀店
candidates.why: The flagship Donki with the Ebisu Tower Ferris wheel. It has every snack, cosmetic, KitKat flavour and character good under one roof, and it stays open late, so it fits after dinner or drinks in Dotonbori. Donki (PPIH) says it has handled refund applications under the new tax-free system without a refund fee since 1 Nov 2026, which makes it one of the best places to hit ¥5,000 excl. tax for a refund. Expect crowded tills; go late.
candidates.best_time: After 21:00, when it is quieter and you are already in Dotonbori
candidates.price: Snacks ¥100–500 each; a ¥5,000+ haul pp is easy
candidates.group_of_8: Split up; each person pays separately with their own passport for tax-free

candidates.name: Daimaru Shinsaibashi (Pokémon Center Osaka DX + depachika)
candidates.name_ja: 大丸心斎橋店（ポケモンセンターオーサカDX・デパ地下）
candidates.why: The Vories-designed department store at the top of Shinsaibashi-suji. Pokémon Center Osaka DX and the Pokémon Café are on 9F, and the B1–B2 food hall is the easiest Minami depachika for boxed sweets as souvenirs. Shinsaibashi PARCO is next door for character shops. Reviews say Pokémon Center DX is crowded at the tills, so go at opening.
candidates.best_time: At 10:00 opening for Pokémon Center; depachika around 18:00–19:00 for markdowns
candidates.booking: Pokémon Café needs a reservation on the official site, released about 31 days ahead; the shop needs none
candidates.group_of_8: Fine; Pokémon Café seats small groups, so book 2 tables of 4

candidates.name: LUCUA Osaka (Nintendo OSAKA, LUCUA 1100)
candidates.why: The young-fashion malls built into JR Osaka Station (LUCUA and LUCUA 1100), with mid-price Japanese brands, BEAMS/United Arrows-type selects, cosmetics, and the Isetan-run beauty floors. Google lists Nintendo OSAKA, Nintendo's official store, on 13F of LUCUA South (the former Daimaru Umeda building). That makes LUCUA the main reason to shop in Umeda as a group, ahead of Grand Front.
candidates.best_time: Weekday late morning; avoid the 25–26 Dec Christmas weekend afternoon
candidates.booking: Nintendo stores can bring in timed-entry tickets on busy days; check the official store page the day before

candidates.name: Grand Front Osaka
candidates.why: A big modern mall north of Osaka Station with mid-to-upper brands, the Umeda Uniqlo/MUJI-type anchors, and a good restaurant floor. It is pleasant but not cheap or distinctive, so give it 45 minutes only if the group is already at LUCUA. The Christmas illumination outside is a free bonus in late December.
candidates.best_time: Evening for the illuminations, after LUCUA

candidates.name: Hankyu Umeda & Hanshin Umeda depachika (souvenirs)
candidates.name_ja: 阪急うめだ本店・阪神梅田本店 デパ地下
candidates.why: The best one-stop souvenir run in Osaka: Hankyu's B1 sweets hall for boxed gifts, and across the street Hanshin's B1 for local grab-and-go such as ika-yaki. Chilled 551 Horai buta-man and Rikuro cheesecake are on sale around Umeda/Osaka Station for taking home. Note that food you eat in Japan is not tax-free, and only sealed gifts you carry out on 29 Dec qualify.
candidates.best_time: 18:00–19:30 for evening markdowns on fresh items; buy shelf-stable boxed gifts on 25–26 Dec, the last Osaka days
candidates.group_of_8: Split up; depachika aisles are tight

candidates.name: Nakazakicho vintage alleys
candidates.why: Pre-war wooden row-houses one stop (or a 10-minute walk) east of Umeda. It is packed with tiny independent vintage shops (the Sakura Building, TAU, olfe.vintage) and cafés. It feels more local and one-of-a-kind than Ame-mura, and is the perfect add-on to an Umeda afternoon. Most shops open at 13:00.
candidates.group_of_8: Narrow alleys and small shops; go in 2 groups of 4

candidates.name: Kyoto Shinkyogoku & Teramachi arcades + Nintendo KYOTO
candidates.name_ja: 新京極・寺町京極商店街／Nintendo KYOTO（京都髙島屋S.C. T8）
candidates.why: Worth 60–90 minutes at the end of a Kyoto sightseeing day, but not a trip of its own: Osaka has more and cheaper. The covered arcades run north from Shijo next to Nishiki Market. SPINNS Kyoto and a vintage cluster are on Teramachi, along with SOU・SOU's Kyoto-made clothing and stamp/stationery shops. Nintendo KYOTO is on 7F of Kyoto Takashimaya S.C. [T8] at the Shijo-Kawaramachi crossing, and Pokémon Center Kyoto is a 10-minute walk west at SUINA Muromachi. Hankyu Kyoto-Kawaramachi station is right there, so take the Hankyu line straight back to Umeda.
candidates.best_time: 16:00–19:00 on the Kyoto day, after the temples close

notes: Osaka · shop: Shopping logic. MINAMI DAY (the main shopping day, best a weekday, 21–24 Dec): Hanshin Namba line Kujō → Osaka-Namba (2 stops) ~10:30 → Den Den Town/Ota Road + Suruga-ya (open 10–11) → walk past Namba Parks → north up Shinsaibashi-suji (drugstores, Daimaru/Pokémon DX, PARCO) → west across Midosuji into Ame-mura (vintage opens ~12–13: Kinji/Big Step first, Triangle Park loop, Mandarake) → Horie Orange Street (JAM) → late Don Quijote Dotonbori after dinner (quiet after 21:00; PPIH says no refund fee). UMEDA HALF-DAY: LUCUA (Nintendo OSAKA 13F) → Grand Front only if time → Nakazakicho vintage from 13:00 → Hankyu/Hanshin depachika 18:00+ for markdowns and boxed souvenirs. KYOTO: Shinkyogoku/Teramachi + Nintendo KYOTO only as the last 60–90 min of a Kyoto day, then Hankyu Kyoto-Kawaramachi → Umeda direct. TIMING: vintage shops rarely open before noon, some close Wednesdays; 25 Dec (Fri) and 26 Dec (Sat) are the most crowded; winter sales start around 1–2 Jan, after Osaka. TAX-FREE (purchases from 1 Nov 2026, refund system): pay the full price incl. 10% tax; minimum ¥5,000 excl. tax per person, per store, per day, with each person's own passport (purchases can't be pooled); refund only after customs confirms export within 90 days, so it is done at Haneda T3 on 29 Dec at the customs kiosk BEFORE bag drop, with every tax-free item in hand (register Visit Japan Web to speed it up); if one item on a receipt is missing or used, the whole receipt loses the refund; snacks and cosmetics used in Japan don't qualify, so buy anything you'll eat or use on a separate receipt; refunds come from the shop or its refund operator (card, app, or airport cash), and fees vary by operator. Leave extra time at Haneda for the kiosk queue.
